text:
Predicates:
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
Blockable(x, y) ::: x can block y's shot.
Jump(x) ::: x can jump when shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.
Shoots(x, y) ::: x shoots at y.
CanBlock(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (Taller(x, y) → Blockable(x, y)) ::: If x is taller than y, then x can block y's shot.
Taller(michael, every-other-person) ::: Michael is taller than everyone else.
∀x ∀y ∀z ((Taller(x, y) ∧ Taller(y, z)) → Taller(x, z)) ::: If x is taller than y, and y is taller than z, then x is taller than z.
Taller(peter, michael) ::: Peter is taller than Michael.
∀x ∀y (Taller(x, y) ∧ Jump(x) → CanBlock(x, y)) ::: If x is taller than y and x can jump, then x can block y's shooting.
¬CanBlock(michael, windy) ::: Michael cannot block Windy's shooting.
∀x (Jump(x) → GreatShooter(x)) ::: Every shooter who can jump is a great shooter.
Conclusion:
CanBlock(peter, windy) ::: Peter can block Windy's shooting.
